title: CVE-2021-22897: schannel cipher selection surprise
excerpt:
## Summary:
[Commit "schannel: support selecting ciphers"](https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/9aefbff30d280c60fc9d8cc3e0b2f19fc70a2f28) added support for selecting the ciphers with SCHANNEL. However, due to use of a static `algIds` array for ciphers in `set_ssl_ciphers` the last configured cipher list will override configuration used by other connections, leading to potential wrong configuration for them. This may have security implications if insecure cipher configuration is used where secure cipher configuration is expected.

## Steps To Reproduce:
 
  1.Create two or more separate curl handles with `curl_easy_init`
  2. Set different cipher lists with `curl_easy_setopt` `CURLOPT_SSL_CIPHER_LIST` to the curl handles
  3. Create simultaneous connections with there the separate curl handles

Instead of each connection using the specific cipher list some of them will share the wrong configuration. If/how this happens exactly depends on how the connection setup overlaps.

Note that to be vulnerable some existing application using libcurl would needs to use such mixed `CURLOPT_SSL_CIPHER_LIST` configuration with multiple curl handles to begin with. It is not really known how likely this really is, but it seems somewhat rare use case.

## Supporting Material/References:
- Commit adding the vulnerable feature: https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/9aefbff30d280c60fc9d8cc3e0b2f19fc70a2f28

## Impact

Potentially wrong cipher configuration used for connections.

summary: The commit added support for selecting ciphers in schannel but used a static algIds array, causing the last configured cipher list to override previous configurations across multiple curl handles, potentially leading to insecure cipher configurations.

claims.text: The static `algIds` array in `set_ssl_ciphers` causes the last configured cipher list to override configuration used by other connections
claims.reasoning: The static array is global to the function. Every call to set_ssl_ciphers writes into the same array, and each connection's SCHANNEL_CRED ends up pointing to that single array. The last caller's cipher list overwrites the array for all connections.

key_reasons: The static ALG_ID algIds[45] array at lib/vtls/schannel.c:335 is shared across all calls to set_ssl_ciphers.
Each connection's SCHANNEL_CRED receives a pointer to this single static array (line 353).
When multiple curl handles configure different cipher lists via CURLOPT_SSL_CIPHER_LIST, the last write overwrites the array for all connections.
This can cause a connection expecting a strong cipher suite to instead use a weaker one configured by another handle, which is a security-relevant misconfiguration.
The bug exists in both the master revision (e540b32562a0) and the release curl-7_76_1 (same static array at line 331).
reply: Thank you for the report. The static `algIds` array in `set_ssl_ciphers` (lib/vtls/schannel.c:335) is indeed shared across all connections using the schannel backend. Each connection's credential points to this single array (line 353), so the last handle to set CURLOPT_SSL_CIPHER_LIST overwrites the cipher list for all concurrent connections. This can cause a connection to use a weaker cipher suite than configured. We will fix this by making the cipher list per-connection (e.g., storing it in SCHANNEL_CRED).
